content.content:
# build.txt Field Reference

## Core Properties

**displayName**
The name displayed when the mod appears in mod lists.

**author**
Display name for mod creator(s). "The author field is just a display value, it doesn't actually control anything."

**version**
Release identifier with format: `<major>.<minor>.<build>.<revision>` (e.g., 1.2.3.4). Must contain 2-4 numbers separated by periods; these "are not decimals," so 1.101 exceeds 1.2.

## Dependency Management

**modReferences**
Required dependencies listed by filename without extension. "This mod will require the dependency mod to be enabled for this mod to be enabled."

**weakReferences**
Optional mod interactions. These mods "don't necessarily have to be enabled" but allow native interoperability if present.

**dllReferences**
Non-mod DLL dependencies, listed by filename without extension. Files must be placed in a `lib/` folder.

## Load Order

**sortAfter**
Mods that force this mod to load after them. "Only affects loading if this mod would normally be loaded before those other mods."

**sortBefore**
Opposite of sortAfter; forces this mod to load before specified mods.

## Content Visibility

**hideCode**
If true, extracted mods exclude .dll, .pdb, and .xml files. Default: false.

**hideResources**
If true, extracted mods exclude asset files (.png, .wav). Default: false.

**includeSource**
If true, includes .cs files when extracting (requires hideResources=false). Default: false.

**buildIgnore**
File patterns to exclude during build. Defaults exclude `build.txt`, dotfiles, `bin/*`, `obj/*`, and `Thumbs.db`.

## Network & Distribution

**side**
"Controls how this mod is synced between client and server." Values: Both (default), Client, Server, NoSync. Determines multiplayer synchronization behavior.

**homepage**
URL for mod's website, displayed in More Info menu alongside Steam Workshop link.

**playableOnPreview**
If false, mod refuses loading on preview tModLoader versions. Default: true.

**translationMod**
If true, mod provides translations for other mods listed in modReferences. Enables automatic localization updates. Default: false.

**noCompile**
If true, uses pre-compiled "ModName.dll" instead of compiling source. Default: false.

I need to verify each API call in the template against the actual ExampleMod and ModLoader source, so I'm listing out the identifiers used—things like item dimensions, damage classes, use animations, knockback, value, and rarity—to grep against the real source.

I'm also checking OnHitNPC's 1.4.4 signature, dust IDs, recipe building with AddIngredient/AddTile/Register, and buff effects like Frostburn2 and OnFire3. One issue stands out: CultistBossLightningOrbArc is a hostile projectile, so spawning it from a player item would actually damage the player instead of enemies—I need to swap it for a friendly projectile type instead.

Since Electrified only applies to players, for NPCs I'll chain SimpleStrikeNPC calls to nearby enemies to simulate chain lightning, and I'm double-checking its full signature including the noPlayerInteraction flag for multiplayer sync. For the teleport/blink mechanic, I'm confirming Player.Teleport's parameters and the TeleportationStyleID options.

For RodOfDiscord-style teleportation I need proper netcode too, using NetMessage.SendData with MessageID.TeleportEntity gated behind the multiplayer client check, since Player.Teleport alone won't sync across clients. I'm also verifying that player.Heal(int) still works as expected in 1.4.4, noting Venom as the poison buff, and sketching out NPC.NewNPC for the summon mechanic.

Then I realize EchoMinion isn't a real type, so that summon call would fail to compile, and NPC.NewNPC called from a client's OnHitNPC wouldn't actually spawn anything useful since NPC spawning needs to run on the server. I'm reconsidering the summon effect entirely — maybe spawning a friendly projectile instead of a minion — and trying to recall which ProjectileIDs actually exist and are marked friendly so I don't invent fake identifiers again.

I settle on TinyEater as a verified friendly homing projectile I could spawn in pairs for a "splits into echoes" effect, but I need to confirm the exact ID name exists in vanilla's ProjectileID since that list isn't on GitHub for me to check directly — I'll instead cross-reference IDs used in ExampleMod's source to make sure each one I pick actually exists.

Checking remaining effects for valid API usage: wingTime/wingTimeMax fields for the flight effect, ShadowFlame for void, Daybreak for the lunar-nighttime trigger, pickSpeed mutation for auto (though it resets each frame so it'd need to live in the right update hook), and AddBuff with Shine for neon — confirming each against real field/buff names before finalizing.

I'm now catching a critical issue: autoloaded ModItem/ModNPC classes require a texture PNG matching their class path, and since this generated mod has no asset files, tModLoader will throw a missing-resource error on load. I need to override the Texture property on each item/NPC to point at an existing vanilla texture path instead, which is a pattern ExampleMod itself uses in several places.

For the NPC specifically, I also need Main.npcFrameCount and AnimationType set to match whatever vanilla sprite sheet I'm borrowing, plus figure out the right way to handle the boss head icon — either through the BossHeadTexture property or via NPCID.Sets rather than the AutoloadBossHead attribute, since that depends on a texture asset that doesn't exist here either.

Town NPCs add more complexity since they need head textures for housing and profiles, so for the "characters" category I think the simpler route is a friendly, non-town NPC — passive AI, friendly flag set, borrowing an existing character's animation and texture (like the Guide), with dialogue handled through GetChat.

I also need to confirm `CanChat()` is what enables talking to non-town NPCs. Beyond that, any generated creature needs a spawn method: normal NPCs need SpawnChance, while bosses need a summon item that calls NPC.SpawnOnPlayer with proper multiplayer-safe netcode, following ExampleMod's pattern. AI logic involving timers or phases also needs netUpdate flags set so it syncs correctly in multiplayer.

For hit effects, I realize the shared effect templates are too generic — things like SOURCE.Teleport or SOURCE.wingTime work fine on NPC in some cases but break on others since NPC lacks certain Player-only members like pickSpeed, and projectile spawning in OnHitPlayer needs to be server-guarded. I'll need to build separate, context-specific effect tables rather than reusing one shared kit across item-on-NPC and NPC-on-player cases.

For ModMount, I'm now checking requirements: it needs textures (possibly optional via ModContent.HasAsset checks), a buff class that must actually exist, a summoning item tied to mountType, and proper LINQ imports for playerYOffsets — following ExampleMount as the reference implementation, including how it handles missing textures and custom visual shaders that require precompiled .xnb effect files.

Given the complexity of custom shaders (Ref<Effect> vs Asset<Effect> differences across versions), a safer route is leveraging existing vanilla screen shaders like FilterMiniTower through ScreenShaderData's string-based constructor rather than compiling a new effect file, similar to how pillar biome filters are registered in vanilla code.

For audio, instead of shipping custom music files that risk breaking MusicLoader lookups, I should default to vanilla MusicID tracks triggered through ModSceneEffect, with clear instructions for swapping in custom .ogg files later.

I'm also noting that TileRunner's signature changed from float to double parameters in 1.4.4, which matters for any worldgen code I write.

Checking GenVars.rockLayer as the correct 1.4.4 path since WorldGen.rockLayer got moved there, confirming PassLegacy's lambda signature from Terraria.GameContent.Generation, and making sure TileID.Amethyst and the required using statements for Terraria.ID and generation namespaces are all accounted for so the worldgen example actually compiles. I'm also second-guessing the naming convention of calling a ModPlayer class "System" since that could confuse people about what it actually inherits from.

I need to guard PostUpdate effects with a myPlayer check to avoid multiplayer desync, and should actually wire the config values into the mod logic rather than leaving them unused, relying on tML's auto-generated localization hjson for display names and tooltips. I'm also worried about namespace requirements matching the mod name, folder naming conventions, and the fact that NUnit test files can't just live inside the mod source without breaking the build -- better to implement a load-time self-check ModSystem instead of a real test suite.

The bigger architectural question is TShock versus tModLoader: these are fundamentally incompatible server types since TShock runs a vanilla OTAPI-based server while tML requires its own loader, and now TShock 6 targets 1.4.5 while tML is still on 1.4.4, so I need to understand which type of server Nxeon's provisioning actually uses before recommending a path.

/**
 * Terraria / TShock image contract, the pinned version and the log parsers —
 * PURE (no I/O), shared by provisioning (lib/game-applier-specs/terraria.ts,
 * lib/terraria-plugins.ts), the update path (worker/terraria-update.ts), the
 * settings applier, the mirror sweep and the drift report.
 *
 * ONE PLACE FOR THE VERSION. To move every NEW Terraria server (and the drift
 * report's reference) to another TShock release, change TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION
 * and make sure that version has a row in TERRARIA_KNOWN_VERSIONS. Nothing else.
 *
 * WHY THE IMAGE CHANGED (2026-10-02). Terraria 1.4.5.8 shipped and the 1.4.5.6
 * clients stopped matching our servers. Every Nxeon Terraria server ran
 * `ryshe/terraria:latest` (sha256:b1c89f7f…, TShock 6.1.0.0 / Terraria 1.4.5.6).
 * That image's TShock line is not maintained: Docker Hub's newest TShock tag is
 * `tshock-1.4.5.6-6.1.0` (2026-03-11); only its VANILLA tags kept moving. TShock's own
 * project publishes an official image, `ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock`, tagged per release
 * (6.2.1 = Terraria 1.4.5.8, published 2026-09-27). Read off the registry with skopeo:
 *
 *   ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock:6.2.1  index sha256:70e59a8e…, linux/amd64 manifest sha256:95e82b0c…,
 *   image id (config digest) sha256:9b5081fd…, ~109 MB compressed, runs as root,
 *   WorkingDir /server, ExposedPorts 7777/tcp 7878/tcp, Volumes /tshock /worlds /plugins,
 *   Entrypoint ./TShock.Server -configpath /tshock -logpath /tshock/logs -crashdir /tshock/crashes
 *              -worldselectpath /worlds -additionalplugins /plugins
 *   (6.0.0, 6.1.0, 6.2.0 and 6.2.1 all carry this identical contract.)
 *
 * CONTAINER CONTRACT, old vs new (verified: ryshe's bootstrap.sh extracted from its layer):
 *
 *                 ryshe/terraria                               ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock
 *   entrypoint    /bin/sh bootstrap.sh                          ./TShock.Server <fixed args above>
 *   world         env WORLD_FILENAME -> `-world <Worlds>/<f>`   args `-world /worlds/<file>` (WE pass it)
 *   worlds dir    /root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds            /worlds
 *   config dir    CONFIGPATH = the Worlds dir (config.json,     /tshock (config.json, tshock.sqlite, logs/)
 *                 tshock.sqlite live NEXT TO the .wld files)
 *   cwd           /tshock  (plugins' "tshock/<f>" -> /tshock/tshock)   /server  (-> /server/tshock)
 *   plugins       /tshock/ServerPlugins (+ our -additionalplugins /tshock/CustomPlugins)   /plugins (flag already in the entrypoint)
 *
 * On our servers all of those host-side paths are the SAME folder, /opt/terraria, so the
 * on-disk layout does not change at all: only the in-container mount points do
 * (terrariaOfficialBinds). config.json therefore stays /opt/terraria/config.json and the
 * existing applier keeps working untouched.
 *
 * COMPATIBILITY (what is and is not established): TShock's 6.2.1 release notes say "replace
 * the files, no data will be lost" and tell people to back up tshock.sqlite and the tshock
 * folder; TShock fills missing config.json keys itself and migrates its own database at
 * startup. Terraria world files are forward compatible within 1.4.x (a newer server loads an
 * older .wld) but NOT backward: once 1.4.5.8 has loaded and saved a world, 1.4.5.6 may not
 * read it. That is why the update backs up the whole folder first and restores it on rollback.
 * No real world was migrated by this change (fakes only).
 */

export const TERRARIA_CONTAINER = "terraria";
export const TERRARIA_IMAGE_REPO = "ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock";

/** The TShock release new servers get and the drift report compares against. ONE-LINE CHANGE. */
export const TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION = "6.2.1";

export type TerrariaKnownVersion = {
  /** TShock release (also the image tag). */
  tshock: string;
  /** Terraria server version it supports (what the game client must match). */
  terraria: string;
  /** Image id (the config digest `docker image inspect` reports), amd64. Verified after every load/pull. */
  imageId: string;
  /** Registry index digest: `docker pull repo@digest` is immutable. */
  indexDigest: string;
  released: string;
};

/**
 * Releases whose image was inspected with skopeo and found to carry the contract above.
 * The mirror sweep (worker/terraria-mirror.ts) reports any newer release that is missing here;
 * add the row it prints. Versions before 6.0.0 are not offered (different Terraria major
 * line, never run on this platform, and a world cannot be taken back to 1.4.4.9).
 */

For requests needing genuinely new content, I'd need tModLoader instead, which requires both server and all players to run 1.4.4 with auto-download, something Nxeon's current TShock servers don't support.

This version adds support for Terraria 1.4.5.8. Thank you so much for all of the hard work that went into this release!

## Notable changes in this release

- Upgraded to OTAPI 3.3.14 for Terraria 1.4.5.8. (@ZakFahey, @bulkinglb, @sors89, @timschumi, @SignatureBeef, @QuiCM, @lost-werewolf)

## Upgrading

**Before installing, make a complete backup of your existing server and all files and folders, including `tshock.sqlite` and the `tshock` folder. We are not responsible for failed installations. Please make sure you backup your data. Severe data loss or gain may occur.**

To upgrade TShock, replace all of the files in the location of your server installation with all of the files from the release zip we provide. Overwrite all files. No data will be lost.

## Docker

Users of Docker may consider using ` docker pull ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock:stable` to get this release. `stable` contains the stable version of TShock.

content.thinking:
Good to confirm TShock.SavePath is the proper way to resolve the plugin's config path, rather than hardcoding "tshock/" like other plugins do. Also noting GeneralHooks.ReloadEvent handles config reload on /reload, and the plugin needs to be compiled as a .dll for Nxeon's install pipeline.

For compiling, I realize the TShock NuGet package (6.2.1) bundles OTAPI, so no proprietary files are needed — we can restore at build time rather than redistributing anything, making a real `dotnet build` harness feasible. I should check if dotnet and docker are available on node-2, since testing could even involve spinning up the official TShock container with the plugin dll mounted to verify server startup logs — mirroring what Nxeon's pipeline already does.

For tModLoader, I recall its GitHub releases legally distribute tModLoader.zip (with Re-Logic's permission), which contains tModLoader.dll but not vanilla Terraria assets — those still require owning the game on Steam. Since compiling only needs the dll and its libs, tML supports a CLI `-build <path>` argument used by modders and CI pipelines, so headless building should be possible without needing the actual game assets.

However, this approach relies on the mod's project file importing a tModLoader.targets file (generated by tML at install) that invokes a BuildMod task to package the .tmod, requiring the .NET 8 SDK. Given the complexity, I should first verify what tooling actually exists on node-2 before committing to this path — the brief wants me to implement it only if nothing proprietary is required, so I'll check feasibility first.

  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,

  # shellcheck disable=SC2086

}

  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail

h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)" != "\$h" ]; then

I'm trying to figure out the correct vanilla mount texture path to use for GetExtraTexture, but I'm unsure of the exact naming convention, so it might be simpler to let the mount load without textures and just have the player ride it invisibly.

I think vanilla mounts handle missing texture layers gracefully with null checks, so I don't need to worry about every texture existing.

Rather than trying to borrow vanilla mount data directly, I should just sketch the main tML generator archetypes instead: items referencing vanilla textures with standard SetDefaults, and for magic-type effects, routing through a ModProjectile or GlobalProjectile since OnHitNPC on the item itself won't trigger for projectile-based attacks.

For magic items, the cleanest approach is a ModProjectile with AIType set to a vanilla projectile so it inherits vanilla behavior, with OnHitNPC applying the custom effect. For accessory-type items (keyed off words like boots, ring, wings, shield), I'm mapping out UpdateAccessory logic — things like damage boosts, movement speed, defense, life regen, fall damage negation, or gravity control depending on the keyword matched.

# tModLoader Installation and Multiplayer Guide

## Installation Requirements

**Steam Installation:**
tModLoader is a separate Steam app. "To install tModLoader on Steam, you need to own Terraria on Steam." The installation exists alongside vanilla, allowing players to run both versions without reinstalling.

**Manual Installation:**
Players can manually install from GitHub releases for GOG or other versions. The guide states: "Unzip the contents of the zip you downloaded to a folder named tModLoader either next to or nested inside the Terraria install folder."

## Version Branches

The guide lists these options:
- **Default/Stable:** Currently based on Terraria 1.4.4.9 content
- **1.3-legacy:** Latest 1.3 release for older mods
- **1.4.3-legacy:** Latest 1.4.3 release
- **preview-v2026.X:** Upcoming changes for testing

"Users can use the beta branches feature of Steam to switch to a legacy or preview version of tModLoader."

## Critical Warning on Mod Compatibility

"If you are switching tModLoader versions to use a particular mod, be aware that other mods you enjoy might not be on the version you switch to, so you might not be able to use all the mods you want together."

## Multiplayer Note

The document states: "these workarounds do not allow for Steam Multiplayer and thus you will need to use IP connect options for multiplayer." This suggests clients need matching mod versions, though explicit auto-download mechanisms aren't detailed.

### tModLoader Mod Upload Rules

The following third-party rules regarding permissible content must be followed
1. the [Steam Subscriber agreement](https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber\_agreement/), 
2. the [Steam Community Rules and Guidelines](https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/6862-8119-C23E-EA7B) and 
3. the [Terraria Rules \& Guidelines](https://forums.terraria.org/index.php?threads/modding-pc-only-rules-guidelines.286/)

In addition, content owners in the tModLoader community are subject to additional rules to ensure a safe environment for the community. Failure to abide by these rules will result in loss of mod publishing privileges. In extreme cases, loss of your Steam account is also a possibility if the infraction also violates the Steam Subscriber agreement. It is to be noted that tModLoader moderators actively report malicious mods to Steam for account deactivation in accordance with the Steam Subscriber agreement. 

These rules apply to all modding content uploaded to the tModLoader community. This includes private and friends only content.

Rule 1: Do not silently sabotage the user's experience

\- Do not destroy the user's world/player/settings etc suddenly and without warning

\- Do not intentionally make tML or other mods appear buggy

\- Mods which are very clearly joke mods may be permitted, as long as it's clear when the joke is happening, and they must not actually destroy files

Rule 2: File system and network access must be sensible

# Major Breaking Changes: tModLoader 1.4.3 to 1.4.4

## Localization System Overhaul

The localization system underwent significant restructuring. According to the guide, developers must migrate from the old approach: `"DisplayName.SetDefault" and "Tooltip.SetDefault removal"` are no longer supported. Instead, mods now use `.hjson` files for localization, representing a fundamental shift in how text content is managed.

## Damage and Hit Hooks Rework

The damage system saw extensive changes. The documentation states: `"Player/NPC damage hooks rework. Hit/HurtModifiers and Hit/HurtInfo"` fundamentally altered how damage calculations work. The `NPC.HitInfo` structure and `HitModifiers` system replaced previous approaches, requiring developers to update any custom damage logic.

## WorldGen Double Precision

Worldgen coordinates shifted from `float` to `double` precision, affecting any mods that manipulate world generation or tile placement at the coordinate level.

## Method and Property Renames

Numerous APIs were renamed for consistency. The guide references `"Renamed or Moved Members"` as a category, though specific renames depend on individual mod implementations.

## tModPorter Tool

The guide introduces `tModPorter`: `"tModPorter is a tool that automatically applies code fixes to mod source code for changes made to tModLoader."` Running this tool is recommended as the first step after updating, though manual fixes may still be required.

## Release Schedule Impact

Mods must be rebuilt monthly under the new release schedule to maintain compatibility with current versions.

/**
 * Terraria modding support for Cyrus (PURE, client-safe, data only). Default export = the GameSupport.
 *
 * Terraria has TWO separate modding worlds and Cyrus picks one per request (lib/cyrus/engine/games/terraria.ts
 * `terrariaFlavor`):
 *
 *   1. TShock server plugins (C#, .NET 9, TerrariaServerAPI). Server-only: players join with the normal game and
 *      install nothing. They can only use what the base game already has (vanilla items, enemies, buffs, events),
 *      because an unmodded game cannot draw new content. THIS IS WHAT NXEON TERRARIA SERVERS RUN TODAY
 *      (lib/terraria-image.ts, official ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock image), and they already have a real one-click
 *      plugin install (worker/game-mods.ts: .dll into /opt/terraria-plugins, restart, confirm TShock's
 *      "Plugin X vY initiated." log line, roll back otherwise).
 *
 *   2. tModLoader content mods (C#, .NET 8). New items, enemies, bosses, biomes, music and visuals. tModLoader is
 *      its own free Steam app (players must own Terraria), the server must run tModLoader, and EVERY player needs
 *      tModLoader too; mods marked side=Both are sent from the server to each player when they join. tModLoader is
 *      still on Terraria 1.4.4.9 (its 1.4.5 port is in progress), so it cannot share a server with a 1.4.5 TShock.
 *      Nxeon does not offer a tModLoader server yet, so these mods are build + download only for now.
 *
 * Every fact below was checked against the loader's own source or release data on 2026-10-08 (see `sources`).
 * The TShock version is NOT duplicated here: it is read from lib/terraria-image.ts (TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION),
 * the one place the platform pins it, so Cyrus always targets exactly what new Nxeon servers run.
 */
import type { GameSupport, GameVersionRule } from "./support";
import { TERRARIA_KNOWN_VERSIONS, TERRARIA_LEGACY_VERSIONS, TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION, terrariaKnown } from "../../terraria-image";

export type TerrariaFlavor = "tshock" | "tmodloader";

/** TShock line facts that do not live in lib/terraria-image.ts (that file pins the release; this maps its major). */
export const TSHOCK_LINES: Record<number, { tsapi: string; dotnet: string; terraria: string }> = {
  // TerrariaServerAPI ServerApi.ApiVersion = 2.1.0.0 at the commit TShock v6.2.1 pins; plugins whose
  // [ApiVersion(major, minor)] differs are skipped with "designed for a different Server API version".
  6: { tsapi: "2.1", dotnet: "net9.0", terraria: "1.4.5" },
  // TShock 5.2.4 NuGet package targets net6.0 (Terraria 1.4.4.9). Never offered on Nxeon (a world cannot go back).
  5: { tsapi: "2.1", dotnet: "net6.0", terraria: "1.4.4" },
};

const pinned = terrariaKnown(TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION);
const pinnedMajor = Number(TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION.split(".")[0]);

/** What a TShock plugin is compiled against: always the platform's pinned release. */
export const TSHOCK_TARGET = {
  tshock: TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION,
  terraria: pinned?.terraria ?? "1.4.5.8",
  tsapi: TSHOCK_LINES[pinnedMajor]?.tsapi ?? "2.1",
  dotnet: TSHOCK_LINES[pinnedMajor]?.dotnet ?? "net9.0",
  /** NuGet package id + version used by the generated .csproj (published by the TShock project, GPL-3.0). */
  nuget: { id: "TShock", version: TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION },
} as const;

/**
 * What a tModLoader mod is built against. Build on STABLE, never preview: tModLoader filters out any mod built for
 * a newer monthly release than the one installed (ModOrganizer: "mod is for a newer tML monthly release"), and most
 * players are on stable. A mod built on an older 1.4.4 month keeps loading on later 1.4.4 months unless the API it
 * uses changed. Update this row when a new stable lands (the first of each month); the readiness checklist has the
 * maintenance steps.
 */
export const TML_TARGET = {
  /** tModLoader stable release Cyrus builds against (GitHub tag, published 2026-10-01). */
  release: "v2026.08.3.0",
  /** The year.month part tModLoader compares ("2026.08"). */
  month: "2026.08",
  /** Terraria content version tModLoader stable is based on. */
  terraria: "1.4.4.9",
  dotnet: "net8.0",
  langVersion: "12.0",
  steamAppId: 1281930,
} as const;

const tshockRows: GameVersionRule[] = [
  ...TERRARIA_KNOWN_VERSIONS.map<GameVersionRule>((k) => ({
    version: `Terraria ${k.terraria} (TShock server)`,
    status: k.tshock === TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION ? "current" : "supported",
    loaderVersion: `TShock ${k.tshock}, TerrariaServerAPI ${TSHOCK_LINES[Number(k.tshock.split(".")[0])]?.tsapi ?? "2.1"}, .NET 9`,
  })),
  {
    version: `Terraria ${TERRARIA_LEGACY_VERSIONS.terraria} (TShock server)`,
    status: "legacy",
    loaderVersion: `TShock ${TERRARIA_LEGACY_VERSIONS.tshock}, TerrariaServerAPI 2.1, .NET 9`,
    breaking: [
      "Older Nxeon Terraria servers still run this until they update. Players on the newest game version cannot join them, so Cyrus builds against the newest TShock and the server should be updated first.",
    ],
  },
  {
    version: "Terraria 1.4.4.9 (TShock server)",
    status: "unsupported",
    loaderVersion: "TShock 5.2.4, .NET 6",
    breaking: [
      "TShock 6 moved to Terraria 1.4.5 and .NET 9. Plugins built for TShock 5 that touch game code changed in 1.4.5 fail when they run, so they must be rebuilt against TShock 6.",
      "A world saved by 1.4.5 cannot be opened by 1.4.4 again, so Nxeon never moves a server back.",
    ],
  },
];

const tmlRows: GameVersionRule[] = [
  {
    version: "Terraria 1.4.4.9 (tModLoader stable)",
    status: "current",
    loaderVersion: `tModLoader ${TML_TARGET.release} (monthly stable), .NET 8`,
  },
  {
    version: "Terraria 1.4.4.9 (tModLoader preview)",
    status: "supported",
    loaderVersion: "tModLoader v2026.09.2.x preview",
    breaking: ["A mod built on preview will not load for players on stable, so Cyrus always builds on stable. Stable mods also load on preview."],
  },
  {
    version: "Terraria 1.4.3 (tModLoader 1.4.3-legacy)",
    status: "legacy",
    loaderVersion: "tModLoader v2022.09.48.x (Steam beta branch 1.4.3-legacy)",
    breaking: [
      "1.4.4 replaced DisplayName.SetDefault/Tooltip.SetDefault with .hjson localization files.",
      "1.4.4 reworked damage hooks (NPC.HitInfo, HitModifiers, Player.HurtInfo), so OnHitNPC and similar have new signatures.",
      "1.4.4 switched world-generation numbers from float to double.",
      "tModLoader keeps 1.4.3 and 1.4.4 mods apart: a mod built for one release stream does not load on the other.",
    ],
  },
  {
    version: "Terraria 1.4.5 (tModLoader port in progress)",
    status: "unsupported",
    loaderVersion: "tModLoader 1.4.5-dev (contributor-only beta, no stable release yet)",
    breaking: ["tModLoader says 1.4.4 mods will not work on its 1.4.5 build without updates. Cyrus will add a 1.4.5 target when tModLoader ships a stable 1.4.5 release."],
  },
];

const support: GameSupport = {
  id: "terraria",
  name: "Terraria",
  builds:
    "Server plugins (TShock) that run on your Nxeon Terraria server with no installs for players, and content mods (tModLoader) that add new weapons, enemies, bosses, biomes, music and visuals.",
  language: "C#",
  loader: {
    name: "TShock (server plugins) and tModLoader (content mods)",
    homepage: "https://github.com/Pryaxis/TShock",
    installDocs: "https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/tModLoader-guide-for-players",
    licenseNote:
      "TShock and its NuGet package are GPL-3.0; tModLoader is MIT. The Terraria game itself is proprietary: Cyrus never ships game files or game art, generated mods only point at art the player's own installed game already has.",
  },
  versions: [...tshockRows, ...tmlRows],
  install: {
    // The default build (TShock plugin) is server-only; tModLoader mods are "both" and say so in clientNote.
    side: "server",
    serverPath: "/opt/terraria-plugins (TShock plugin .dll). tModLoader mods go in tModLoader/Mods with an enabled.json entry.",
    clientNote:
      "Server plugins: players install nothing and join with the normal game. Content mods: every player needs tModLoader (a free app on Steam for anyone who owns Terraria). When they join, the server sends them the mod automatically, and tModLoader shows a warning that the mod is not from the Steam Workshop; they accept it and the game reloads.",
    needsRestart: true,
    hotReload: false,
    packaging: "dll",
    reason:
      "Most requests become a server plugin: it runs on the server only, so it works with the normal game and nobody has to install anything. New items, enemies, bosses, biomes and visuals need a content mod instead, which every player must also run.",
  },
  verification: {
    method: "compile",
    notes:
      "Every generated mod first passes Cyrus's static checks (lib/cyrus/games/terraria.validate.ts). On the build host, a TShock plugin compiles with the .NET 9 SDK against the public TShock NuGet package, and a tModLoader mod compiles with the .NET 8 toolchain against the public tModLoader release, which builds the real .tmod file. Neither needs any game file. Not done yet: a live load-test on a throwaway server and an automatic build step in the Cyrus pipeline (see READINESS.md).",
    canRunSandbox: false,

/**
 * Terraria modding support for Cyrus (PURE, client-safe, data only). Default export = the GameSupport.
 *
 * Terraria has TWO separate modding worlds and Cyrus picks one per request (lib/cyrus/engine/games/terraria.ts
 * `terrariaFlavor`):
 *
 *   1. TShock server plugins (C#, .NET 9, TerrariaServerAPI). Server-only: players join with the normal game and
 *      install nothing. They can only use what the base game already has (vanilla items, enemies, buffs, events),
 *      because an unmodded game cannot draw new content. THIS IS WHAT NXEON TERRARIA SERVERS RUN TODAY
 *      (lib/terraria-image.ts, official ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock image), and they already have a real one-click
 *      plugin install (worker/game-mods.ts: .dll into /opt/terraria-plugins, restart, confirm TShock's
 *      "Plugin X vY initiated." log line, roll back otherwise).
 *
 *   2. tModLoader content mods (C#, .NET 8). New items, enemies, bosses, biomes, music and visuals. tModLoader is
 *      its own free Steam app (players must own Terraria), the server must run tModLoader, and EVERY player needs
 *      tModLoader too; mods marked side=Both are sent from the server to each player when they join. tModLoader is
 *      still on Terraria 1.4.4.9 (its 1.4.5 port is in progress), so it cannot share a server with a 1.4.5 TShock.
 *      Nxeon does not offer a tModLoader server yet, so these mods are build + download only for now.
 *
 * Every fact below was checked against the loader's own source or release data on 2026-10-08 (see `sources`).
 * The TShock version is NOT duplicated here: it is read from lib/terraria-image.ts (TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION),
 * the one place the platform pins it, so Cyrus always targets exactly what new Nxeon servers run.
 */
import type { GameSupport, GameVersionRule } from "./support";
import { TERRARIA_KNOWN_VERSIONS, TERRARIA_LEGACY_VERSIONS, TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION, terrariaKnown } from "../../terraria-image";

export type TerrariaFlavor = "tshock" | "tmodloader";

/** TShock line facts that do not live in lib/terraria-image.ts (that file pins the release; this maps its major). */
export const TSHOCK_LINES: Record<number, { tsapi: string; dotnet: string; terraria: string }> = {
  // TerrariaServerAPI ServerApi.ApiVersion = 2.1.0.0 at the commit TShock v6.2.1 pins; plugins whose
  // [ApiVersion(major, minor)] differs are skipped with "designed for a different Server API version".
  6: { tsapi: "2.1", dotnet: "net9.0", terraria: "1.4.5" },
  // TShock 5.2.4 NuGet package targets net6.0 (Terraria 1.4.4.9). Never offered on Nxeon (a world cannot go back).
  5: { tsapi: "2.1", dotnet: "net6.0", terraria: "1.4.4" },
};

const pinned = terrariaKnown(TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION);
const pinnedMajor = Number(TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION.split(".")[0]);

/** What a TShock plugin is compiled against: always the platform's pinned release. */
export const TSHOCK_TARGET = {
  tshock: TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION,
  terraria: pinned?.terraria ?? "1.4.5.8",
  tsapi: TSHOCK_LINES[pinnedMajor]?.tsapi ?? "2.1",
  dotnet: TSHOCK_LINES[pinnedMajor]?.dotnet ?? "net9.0",
  /** NuGet package id + version used by the generated .csproj (published by the TShock project, GPL-3.0). */
  nuget: { id: "TShock", version: TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION },
} as const;

/**
 * What a tModLoader mod is built against. Build on STABLE, never preview: tModLoader filters out any mod built for
 * a newer monthly release than the one installed (ModOrganizer: "mod is for a newer tML monthly release"), and most
 * players are on stable. A mod built on an older 1.4.4 month keeps loading on later 1.4.4 months unless the API it
 * uses changed. Update this row when a new stable lands (the first of each month); the readiness checklist has the
 * maintenance steps.
 */
export const TML_TARGET = {
  /** tModLoader stable release Cyrus builds against (GitHub tag, published 2026-10-01). */
  release: "v2026.08.3.0",
  /** The year.month part tModLoader compares ("2026.08"). */
  month: "2026.08",
  /** Terraria content version tModLoader stable is based on. */
  terraria: "1.4.4.9",
  dotnet: "net8.0",
  langVersion: "12.0",
  steamAppId: 1281930,
} as const;

const tshockRows: GameVersionRule[] = [
  ...TERRARIA_KNOWN_VERSIONS.map<GameVersionRule>((k) => ({
    version: `Terraria ${k.terraria} (TShock server)`,
    status: k.tshock === TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION ? "current" : "supported",
    loaderVersion: `TShock ${k.tshock}, TerrariaServerAPI ${TSHOCK_LINES[Number(k.tshock.split(".")[0])]?.tsapi ?? "2.1"}, .NET 9`,
  })),
  {
    version: `Terraria ${TERRARIA_LEGACY_VERSIONS.terraria} (TShock server)`,
    status: "legacy",
    loaderVersion: `TShock ${TERRARIA_LEGACY_VERSIONS.tshock}, TerrariaServerAPI 2.1, .NET 9`,
    breaking: [
      "Older Nxeon Terraria servers still run this until they update. Players on the newest game version cannot join them, so Cyrus builds against the newest TShock and the server should be updated first.",
    ],
  },
  {
    version: "Terraria 1.4.4.9 (TShock server)",
    status: "unsupported",
    loaderVersion: "TShock 5.2.4, .NET 6",
    breaking: [
      "TShock 6 moved to Terraria 1.4.5 and .NET 9. Plugins built for TShock 5 that touch game code changed in 1.4.5 fail when they run, so they must be rebuilt against TShock 6.",
      "A world saved by 1.4.5 cannot be opened by 1.4.4 again, so Nxeon never moves a server back.",
    ],
  },
];

    breaking: ["tModLoader says 1.4.4 mods will not work on its 1.4.5 build without updates. Cyrus will add a 1.4.5 target when tModLoader ships a stable 1.4.5 release."],
  },
];

Yoyo works fine with vanilla textures, so I'll plan weapon categories like sword, yoyo, ranged, and magic, then write the generator carefully to handle C# syntax correctly inside the template literals.

I'm checking how string interpolation and code-block formatting rules work to avoid collisions, then planning the TML context interface along with the mod's internal naming convention and config class naming.

Now I'm realizing the config dependency is tricky: if Katara only ships three files without a config file, the main code can't reference a config class that doesn't exist. I'm working out that for Katara, constants should live in a static class inside the main file itself, while other models can split config into its own file, so I need to branch the generator logic based on `input.model`.

This gives nice symmetry: `Tuning.Power` works whether Tuning is a static type with constants or a property returning a config instance. But I need to check timing — configs must be loaded before SetDefaults runs for item.damage = Tuning.Damage to work correctly, so I should verify ModConfig initialization order relative to content loading.

Given the risk, I'll stick with literal numbers in SetDefaults and reserve config-driven values for runtime effect parameters like power, duration, and radius, with reasonable DefaultValue and Range attributes on each field. ServerSide configs sync to clients, while anything purely cosmetic (UI, audio, shaders) should be ClientSide instead.

Fields need to be public with proper localization labels in hjson, falling back to tML's auto-generated entries if I omit them. For the actual hit effects, I'm mapping each elemental type to its corresponding buff application inside OnHitNPC, grabbing the owning player via Projectile.owner when the hit comes from a projectile rather than an item.

Writing chain lightning logic...

I'm checking that chained strikes using SimpleStrikeNPC won't recursively trigger item OnHitNPC, avoiding infinite loops, and noting it correctly sets interaction flags. For the teleport-blink effect, I'm making sure it only runs on the local player's client and positioning the blink point behind the target.

Still, I realize I need a cooldown so the blink doesn't fire on every single hit—without a ModPlayer to store state, I'm considering simpler alternatives like a static field tied to the item.

I'm also adding a chance parameter so blink and summon effects only trigger probabilistically, and healing a percentage of damage dealt—but I need to guard against double-healing in multiplayer by only calling it on the local player, and I'm wary that uncapped lifesteal could be overpowered compared to vanilla's budgeted lifesteal mechanic.

For the summon effect, I'm spawning a couple of TinyEater projectiles at the target with scaled-down damage, owned by the hitting player, and checking how vanilla syncs locally-spawned projectiles across the network to make sure this fires correctly in multiplayer.

For flight, autofire, and neon effects, I'm applying buffs like Featherfall, Mining, and Shine to the local player for the effect's duration, gated behind a check that the player is the local client.

Midas targets an NPC to apply a coin-dropping buff, which should sync through NPC.AddBuff's client-to-server packet. For visual flair, I'm matching dust types to each effect — ice torch dust for frost, electric dust for storm, magic mirror dust for blink, and so on — though some less common dust IDs like Venom or BlueFairy need verifying at compile time.

Now I'm working out the player-hit side: when an NPC strikes a player, the corresponding effect buff applies to that player instead — Chilled or Frostburn for frost, OnFire for fire, Electrified for storm, Confused for blink, with Bleeding and Venom-style debuffs standing in for heal and poison since healing the NPC itself doesn't make sense on the hit-player side.

I'm mapping the remaining variants onto existing player debuffs too — Slow for summon and flight types, Weak for auto, Darkness for void, MoonLeech for lunar, Confused for neon — and noting that durations should be shorter for players than for NPCs. I'm also confirming that this logic belongs in OnHitPlayer, applied via AddBuff on the hit player directly, while the beneficial self-buffs get applied periodically through the ModPlayer's own update logic. Now I'm starting to sketch the enemy NPC class definition itself.

Setting other spawn chances for slime variants, accounting for hardmode conditions, then adding loot drop rules in ModifyNPCLoot...

For base AI styles, I'm mapping slime-types to BlueSlime, bats to CaveBat, flying enemies to DemonEye, and defaulting others to Skeleton or Zombie. For the split-on-death effect, I'm having the NPC spawn two smaller slimes server-side on kill using NPC.NewNPC, mirroring the classic slime split mechanic.

I'll skip the boss head icon since the asset path isn't certain, and leave the town NPC as a friendly wanderer without extra complexity. Now I'm moving on to writing the generator file and the TShock plugin code with careful attention to C# correctness.

Setting up the plugin class with its name, version, permissions, config path, and a settings object, along with a dictionary tracking last-use timestamps per player index...

I'm designing a Settings class with JSON serialization, loading defaults and writing the config file safely within TShock's save path, confirming Newtonsoft.Json is available transitively through TSAPI, and checking that TShock.Log exposes a ConsoleError method for logging failures.

Now I'm sketching out the different command modules: a radius-based "power" command with cooldown, an "enchant" mode tied to NpcStrike hooks checking held items and permissions, a "rewards" system triggered on boss kills that broadcasts and distributes loot, and a "welcome" feature that greets first-time joiners and tracks them persistently in a JSON file, possibly granting a starter kit.

I'm also planning a "bossrush" admin command that spawns a sequence of vanilla boss NPCs near the player and tracks kills to progress through the sequence, plus working out the specific TShock-side effect implementations like applying frostburn debuffs with buff sync packets and strike-based damage effects.

For the remaining effects, I'm mapping out heal using TSPlayer.Heal, blink via teleporting the player just above the target NPC, flight using the featherfall buff, and sketching out auto-mining and neon/Midas-touch effects, while still deciding how to handle the summon effect.

For summon, spawning a server-owned friendly TinyEater projectile with the player as owner seems risky since the client could misinterpret ownership and kill it immediately. I'm leaning toward reworking summon into a "rally" effect that grants nearby players Wrath and Rage buffs instead, though I note this diverges from the kit's advertised label about echoes fighting alongside the player, which would make that description misleading.

On a dedicated server Main.myPlayer is 255, so server-owned projectile damage calculations would actually execute server-side, but I'm uncertain whether that behaves safely as friendly-only, so I should avoid relying on it. Rather than compromise on honesty with a mismatched label, I need to pick a concrete TShock-compatible way to spawn the "echoes" that actually fight alongside the player.

For TShock I'll implement echoes as two extra spectral strikes on the target for half damage each, approximating "splits into echoes" even though it's a stretch for "fight alongside" — I'll note in the docs that on a server plugin these are just extra spectral hits rather than actual summoned allies. I also need to handle strike-hook frequency with a per-player cooldown and chance-based trigger, using the player's index for tracking.

I'm worried that applying a strike inside the NpcStrike handler could re-trigger the same hook recursively, since the hook likely fires from the underlying NPC strike event for any damage source — so I need a thread-static re-entrancy guard to prevent infinite recursion when chaining strikes. For the "power" command mode, I'll loop over nearby NPCs in a radius to apply the effect, and for the rewards mode I'm sketching the NpcKilled handler to check whether the kill qualifies (boss or all-enemies setting) before granting rewards.

For boss kills, I'm planning to iterate active TShock players and give each one the configured reward item and stack via GiveItem, with a broadcast announcement. Multi-segment bosses like Eater of Worlds complicate this since each segment death could fire separately, so I need to dedupe using the NPC's realLife field to only reward once when the true boss entity dies, though EoW's distributed segment structure makes this tricky and may require checking if any NPCs of that type remain active after a death.

For first-join welcome messages, I'll use the NetGreetPlayer hook and track seen players by name in a persisted JSON file, then follow up with a kit of starter items. 146:## 5. Terraria: tModLoader and TShock
147-
148-### 5.1 Platform snapshot [V: GitHub APIs, 2026-10-08]
149-- **tModLoader** is MIT. Stable `v2026.08.3.0` (2026-10-01) targets **Terraria 1.4.4**; a preview `v2026.09.2.1` is also 1.4.4. A `1.4.5` branch is under active development (commits on 2026-10-07). Monthly-style version tags and a long "Update Migration Guide" with one section per month show a fast breaking-change cadence, and `tModPorter` exists to help port [V: [wiki](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/Update-Migration-Guide)]. Needs the **.NET 8 SDK** (.NET 9 and 10 explicitly "will not work") [V: [developer guide](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/tModLoader-guide-for-developers)].
150-- **TShock** (server mod, vanilla clients can join) `6.2.1` (2026-09-27) targets **Terraria 1.4.5.8**; earlier 6.x covered 1.4.5.5 and 1.4.5.6 [V]; 5.2.x covered 1.4.4.9 [S: one fetch summary]. Built on OTAPI; building needs the .NET 9 SDK [V: [TShock README](https://github.com/Pryaxis/TShock)].
151-- **Sides.** tML content mods must be on server **and** every client at the same versions; a mismatch blocks joining; clients are usually prompted to download missing mods [S: [FragNet](https://kb.fragnet.net/Games/Terraria/How_to_add_mods_to_your_tModLoader_server/), [Falix](https://client.falixnodes.net/guides/game-servers/terraria-tmodloader-mods), several others]. TShock needs nothing on the client [I, consistent with its design as a server plugin host].
152-- **Server install for tML:** `.tmod` files plus `enabled.json` in the server's Mods folder, or a management script that installs from a Workshop-exported `install.txt` [V: [Starting a modded server](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/Starting-a-modded-server); the page notes it is outdated for 1.4.4 dedicated servers and points to the `DedicatedServerUtils` readme].
153-
154-### 5.2 Mod anatomy (tML) [V: [Basic Modding Guide](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/Basic-tModLoader-Modding-Guide)]
155-`build.txt` (display name, author, version), `description.txt`, `.csproj`, one `Mod` class, content classes (`ModItem`, `ModNPC`, `ModProjectile`, `ModTile`, `ModBuff`, `ModPlayer`, `ModSystem`, `GlobalItem`, ...), localisation in `Localization/en-US_Mods.<Name>.hjson`, `icon.png` (80x80) and `icon_small.png` (30x30). Output is a `.tmod` file built with Build + Reload.
156-
157-**Textures are autoloaded by class path:** a PNG next to the `.cs` with the same name as the class. "Items, Projectiles, and NPC all need a texture... any one of these without an associated texture will cause your mod to be unable to load" [V: [Basic Autoload](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/Basic-Autoload)]. This is a concrete hazard for any AI generator that emits an item without art.
158-
159-### 5.3 What advanced looks like (tML)
160-
161-| Capability | Technique | AI today |
162-|---|---|---|
163-| Weapons, armour, accessories, buffs | `ModItem` hooks, `ModPlayer` for set bonuses, `GlobalItem` to change vanilla; recipes in `ModItem.AddRecipes` or `ModSystem.AddRecipes` [V: [recipes](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/Basic-Recipes)] | R1 to R2 |
164-| Minions and projectiles | Custom AI via `ModProjectile.AI`, buff-plus-minion pattern | R2 |
165-| NPCs and bosses | `ModNPC` AI states, spawn conditions, loot via `ModifyNPCLoot` | R2 simple, R3 boss fights (balance and telegraphing) |
166-| Tiles and tile entities | Framed tiles, `ModTileEntity`, placement and mining rules | R3 (sprite frames and hitboxes are fussy) |
167-| World generation | `ModSystem.ModifyWorldGenTasks`, reference the vanilla step list [V: wiki index lists World Generation and Vanilla World Generation Steps] | R3 |
168-| Custom UI | `UIState` via `ModSystem` interface layers | R2/R3 |
169-| Config | `ModConfig` (JSON-backed, server-synced) | R1 |
170-| Saving data | `TagCompound` in `SaveData/LoadData` [V: wiki index "Saving and loading"] | R1 |
171-| Cross-mod support | `Mod.Call`, weak references [V: wiki index "Expert Cross Mod Content"] | R2 |
172-| Patching vanilla | IL editing and detours with MonoMod [V: wiki index "Expert IL Editing", "Advanced Detouring"] | R3, and it breaks every Terraria update |
173-| Shaders | Armour dyes and screen shaders [V: wiki index] | R3 |
174-
175-### 5.4 Netcode (the usual multiplayer killer)
176-- Three flows: client to server to clients, client to server, server to client. Use `ModPacket` and `HandlePacket`; keep packets small; prefer deterministic logic so less must be sent [V: [Intermediate netcode](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/wiki/Intermediate-netcode)].
177-- "If a mod is actually buggy during multiplayer, it is often because they do not send packets at all and clients aren't synchronized" [V, same page]. AI-generated tML mods that were only reasoned about in single player will desync. A validator can at least flag state mutated in `Update` hooks with no sync call.
178-
179-### 5.5 TShock (server plugin) techniques
180-- Plugins are .NET DLLs on OTAPI; "you have direct access to all public fields in the `Terraria` namespace" [V: TShock README]. Typical advanced work: command suites, permission groups, region protection, event rewards, anti-cheat tuning, scheduled events, per-group item rules.
181-- It cannot add items or art (vanilla clients do not have them), so "custom item" requests belong to tML, not TShock.
182-- Decompiled server sources are maintained by the TShock team for contributors [V README]; they are proprietary-derived, so Cyrus must not ship them.
183-
184-### 5.6 Pitfalls
185-- Wrong .NET SDK (8 vs 9) [V]. Texture and class name mismatches [V]. Missing localisation keys [I].
186-- "Mod not fully unloaded" memory leaks from static references; the wiki has a dedicated page [V: index link].
--
191:### 5.7 What AI can and cannot do (Terraria)
192-- **R1:** a `ModItem` with stats and a recipe, buffs, simple `ModConfig`, TShock commands. The official ExampleMod (MIT) is a strong golden reference; tML `ExampleMod` ships in the repo [V: [ExampleMod](https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/tree/stable/ExampleMod)].
193-- **R2:** projectiles, minions, simple NPCs, UI panels. Needs compile against the real tML assemblies and a load test.
194-- **R3:** bosses, tiles, world gen, IL editing, netcode design, sprite frames. A compile check cannot tell if the game plays well.
195-- Verification: tML can run a headless dedicated server on Linux with the management script [V], so a load-and-join smoke test is plausible. It needs the game's licensed files via SteamCMD, which Cyrus must not redistribute; the Terraria agent owns this call.
196-
197----
198-
199-## 6. Valheim: BepInEx and Jotunn
200-
201-### 6.1 Platform snapshot
202-- **Valheim 1.0 shipped 2026-09-09** and "mods broke initially"; Iron Gate said they "cannot guarantee that any mods will be functional" [S: [HostHavoc](https://hosthavoc.com/blog/valheim-1-0-update-server-owners) and the GameServerKings 1.0 guide]. BepInExPack_Valheim `5.4.2351` (2026-09-24) and Jotunn `2.30.2` (2026-09-21) are current [V: Thunderstore API, GitHub API]. Jotunn 2.30.0 notes: "Updated the majority of systems for Valheim 1.0.7... Piece categories are not updated yet, Valheim overhauled the system completely. Custom pieces show up in the build menu, but don't have a category" [V: [release 2.30.0](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn/releases/tag/v2.30.0)].
203-- **Engine:** Unity **6000.0.61** for asset work [V: [Jotunn asset-creation tutorial](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn/blob/prod/JotunnLib/Documentation/tutorials/asset-creation.md)].
204-- **Language / loader:** C# plugins on BepInEx (LGPL-2.1) with Harmony patches; Jotunn is MIT [prior research; Jotunn MIT re-verified via API]. Jotunn supplies entity wrappers: `CustomItem`, `CustomPiece`, `CustomRecipe`, `CustomCreature`, `CustomStatusEffect`, `CustomLocation`, `CustomVegetation`, `CustomItemConversion`, `KitbashObject`, `Mocks`, plus managers for commands, GUI, input, localisation, minimap, skills, zones, rendering, undo and network sync [V: [Jotunn README](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn)].
205-- **Sides.** Mods are server-side only, client-side only, or both; for "both", the client and server must have matching files or the handshake refuses [S: [Hosthavoc](https://hosthavoc.com/de-DE/wiki/game-servers/valheim/install-bepinex), [Berrybyte](https://berrybyte.net/wiki/games/valheim/best-mods)]. Jotunn's `NetworkCompatibility` attribute enforces this: levels `NotEnforced`, `VersionCheckOnly`, `EveryoneMustHaveMod`, `ClientMustHaveMod`, `ServerMustHaveMod`, with `VersionStrictness` (major/minor/patch semantics) [V: [NetworkCompatibility tutorial](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn/blob/prod/JotunnLib/Documentation/tutorials/networkcompatibility.md)]. This is the exact data Cyrus's `GameSupport.install.side` needs.
206-
207-### 6.2 What advanced looks like
208-
209-| Capability | Technique | AI today |
210-|---|---|---|
211-| Config-synced balance mods | BepInEx `ConfigEntry` with Jotunn config sync (`SynchronizationManager`) | R1 |
212-| New items by cloning vanilla | `PrefabManager.OnVanillaPrefabsAvailable` then `CustomItem(name, basePrefab, config)`; edit the cloned `ItemDrop` stats; add a `CustomRecipe` [V: Jotunn items tutorial + docs layout] | R1 to R2 |
213-| New icons without a Unity project | `RenderManager` renders a prefab to a sprite at runtime; `AssetUtils.LoadSpriteFromFile`, `LoadTexture`, `LoadMesh` (OBJ) load from files [V: [render queue](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn/blob/prod/JotunnLib/Documentation/tutorials/renderqueue.md), `AssetUtils.cs`] | R2 (a no-Unity art path) |
214-| Status effects and skills | `CustomStatusEffect`, `SkillManager` | R2 |
215-| Creatures | Clone and edit vanilla creatures; new rigs need Unity | R2 clone, R3 new |
216-| Build pieces | `CustomPiece` with a piece table and category (broken for categories in 1.0.7 [V]) | R2, version-fragile |
217-| World content | `CustomLocation`/`CustomVegetation` via `ZoneManager`. A zone is 64 by 64 m and holds **one** location, so the number of location slots is limited [V: [zones](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn/blob/prod/JotunnLib/Documentation/tutorials/zones.md)] | R3 |
218-| Networking | `NetworkManager.CustomRPC` compresses and splits big payloads; use ZNetView RPCs for small per-object data [V: [RPCs](https://github.com/Valheim-Modding/Jotunn/blob/prod/JotunnLib/Documentation/tutorials/rpcs.md)] | R2/R3 |
219-| Compatibility with other mods | `ModCompatibility`, mod registry, soft dependencies via `BepInDependency` [V: file listing; usage [I]] | R2 |
220-| New assets | Author prefabs in a Unity 6000.0.61 project that holds the game's components, build an AssetBundle, load it in the plugin [V] | R3 |
221-
222-### 6.3 Pitfalls
223-- 1.0 broke systems wholesale (piece categories); a mod generated against pre-1.0 docs will compile and misbehave [V].
224-- Cloned objects: references to vanilla prefabs resolve at runtime through Jotunn "Mocks" [V]; a hand-built prefab that references vanilla materials directly can end up with pink or missing shaders [I].
225-- `ZNetView.m_persistent` must be true for objects to save [V: zones tutorial]. Missing it means objects vanish.
226-- Unity version lock: bundles must be built with the exact Unity version the game uses [V]. Wrong version means the bundle refuses to load.
227-- Harmony patches on internals break whenever the method signature changes [I].
228-- Dedicated-server load of client-only code (UI) throws; guard with `ZNet.instance.IsDedicated()` style checks [I].
229-
230-### 6.4 What AI can and cannot do (Valheim)
231-- **R1:** config-and-stat mods, recipe tweaks, clone-and-modify items, status effects, console commands, with a per-version API sheet taken from the game's decompiled assemblies and the Jotunn docs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cyrus · Terraria compile check. Compiles every mod in a matrix written by scripts/cyrus/terraria-matrix.ts
# against the REAL loaders, using only public downloads (no game files):
#   - TShock plugins: .NET 9 SDK + the TShock NuGet package (TSHOCK_VERSION, GPL-3.0) -> <Name>.dll
#   - tModLoader mods: .NET 8 SDK + the public tModLoader release zip (MIT) -> <Mod>.tmod, packaged by tModLoader's
#     own `-build` step (the same code path as the in-game "Build + Reload").
# Run it on the build host only (node-2), e.g. from a worktree:
#   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run --lock -- bash scripts/cyrus/terraria-compile-check.sh
# Tools are installed once into $TOOLS (default /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-terraria-tools) by --setup.
set -uo pipefail

TOOLS="${TOOLS:-/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-terraria-tools}"
TML_RELEASE="${TML_RELEASE:-v2026.08.3.0}"
OUT="${OUT:-/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-terraria-matrix}"
ONLY="${ONLY:-}"   # optional substring filter on the mod folder name

setup() {
  mkdir -p "$TOOLS" && cd "$TOOLS" || exit 1
  [ -f dotnet-install.sh ] || curl -fsSL -o dotnet-install.sh https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh
  [ -x dotnet/dotnet ] || bash dotnet-install.sh --channel 9.0 --install-dir "$TOOLS/dotnet"
  [ -x dotnet8/dotnet ] || bash dotnet-install.sh --channel 8.0 --install-dir "$TOOLS/dotnet8"
  if [ ! -f "tml-$TML_RELEASE/tModLoader.dll" ]; then
    curl -fsSL -o "tModLoader-$TML_RELEASE.zip" "https://github.com/tModLoader/tModLoader/releases/download/$TML_RELEASE/tModLoader.zip"
    python3 -c "import zipfile,sys; zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "tModLoader-$TML_RELEASE.zip" "tml-$TML_RELEASE"
  fi
}

[ "${1:-}" = "--setup" ] && { setup; exit 0; }
setup >/dev/null

export DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 DOTNET_NOLOGO=1 DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1
export NUGET_PACKAGES="$TOOLS/nuget"

# 1) fresh matrix from the generator in this worktree
npx tsx scripts/cyrus/terraria-matrix.ts "$OUT" >/dev/null || { echo "matrix generation failed"; exit 1; }

pass=0; fail=0; failed=()

# 2) TShock plugins
for d in "$OUT"/tshock/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$d"); [ -n "$ONLY" ] && [[ "$name" != *"$ONLY"* ]] && continue
  # The yakko self-check file is optional; it compiles with the plugin when present.
  log="$d/build.log"
  if (cd "$d" && "$TOOLS/dotnet/dotnet" build -c Release -nologo -v q >"$log" 2>&1) && [ -f "$d/bin/Release/net9.0/$name.dll" ]; then
    echo "PASS tshock $name"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    echo "FAIL tshock $name"; grep -E "error|Error" "$log" | sort -u | head -12; fail=$((fail+1)); failed+=("tshock/$name")
  fi
done

# 3) tModLoader mods: ModSources/<Mod> + ModSources/tModLoader.targets, then `dotnet build` which compiles and
#    calls `tModLoader.dll -server -build` to package the .tmod (BuildMod target in tMLMod.targets).
TML="$TOOLS/tml-$TML_RELEASE"
printf '<Project ToolsVersion="14.0" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/developer/msbuild/2003">\n  <Import Project="%s/tMLMod.targets" />\n</Project>\n' "$TML" >"$OUT/tml/tModLoader.targets"
export PATH="$TOOLS/dotnet8:$PATH" DOTNET_ROOT="$TOOLS/dotnet8"
for d in "$OUT"/tml/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$d"); [ -n "$ONLY" ] && [[ "$name" != *"$ONLY"* ]] && continue
  log="$d/build.log"
  # Katara output has no .csproj (the in-game builder does not need one); give the harness the standard one.
  [ -f "$d/$name.csproj" ] || printf '<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">\n  <Import Project="..\\tModLoader.targets" />\n  <PropertyGroup>\n    <AssemblyName>%s</AssemblyName>\n    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>\n  </PropertyGroup>\n</Project>\n' "$name" >"$d/$name.csproj"
  if (cd "$d" && dotnet build -nologo -v q >"$log" 2>&1) && grep -q "Build mod complete\|Building $name\|Packaging" "$log" 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(find "$d" "$HOME/.local/share/Terraria/tModLoader/Mods" -maxdepth 1 -name "$name.tmod" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then
    if grep -qE "error CS|error :|: error" "$log"; then
      echo "FAIL tml $name"; grep -E "error" "$log" | sort -u | head -12; fail=$((fail+1)); failed+=("tml/$name")
    else
      echo "PASS tml $name"; pass=$((pass+1))
    fi
  else
    echo "FAIL tml $name"; grep -E "error|Error|Exception" "$log" | sort -u | head -12; fail=$((fail+1)); failed+=("tml/$name")
  fi
done

echo "----"
echo "compile check: $pass passed, $fail failed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || { printf '  %s\n' "${failed[@]}"; exit 1; }

## Cyrus · Terraria modding support (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-terraria`)

Terraria has two separate modding worlds and Cyrus now picks one per request (`terrariaFlavor` in
`lib/cyrus/engine/games/terraria.ts`):

| | TShock server plugin | tModLoader content mod |
|---|---|---|
| What it can do | commands, permissions, hooks on hits/kills/joins, vanilla items/enemies/bosses/buffs | new items, enemies, bosses, mounts, world gen, UI, music, screen effects |
| Game version | Terraria 1.4.5.8 (TShock 6.2.1, TerrariaServerAPI 2.1, .NET 9) | Terraria 1.4.4.9 (tModLoader v2026.08.3.0 stable, .NET 8) |
| Players install | nothing | tModLoader (free Steam app); the server sends the mod on join |
| Runs on Nxeon today | yes: `/opt/terraria-plugins`, existing restart-and-verify installer | no: Nxeon Terraria servers run TShock; needs a tModLoader server variant |

- **Facts file:** `lib/cyrus/games/terraria.ts` (GameSupport, with `knowledge.apiSheet` + `failureRules`). The TShock
  target is read from `lib/terraria-image.ts` `TERRARIA_PINNED_VERSION`, so plugins always target what new servers run;
  a test fails if the pinned TShock major has no `TSHOCK_LINES` row. The tModLoader target (`TML_TARGET`) is updated by
  hand when a new stable ships (always build on stable: tModLoader skips mods built for a newer monthly release).
- **Generator:** `lib/cyrus/engine/games/terraria.ts`, wired into `buildModFiles` only for `game.id === "terraria"`
  (user-added tModLoader-style games keep the old generic template). Outputs `cyrus.mod.json` (flavor, target versions,
  side, playersInstall, install path, permissions/commands) plus `build.txt`/`.csproj`/hjson localization (tML) or
  `.csproj` + settings JSON (TShock). Content mods point at the player's own game art (`Terraria/Images/Item_N`) so they
  always load; nothing proprietary is shipped. Katara's three files are a complete project.
- **Validator:** `lib/cyrus/games/terraria.validate.ts` `validateTerraria(files)` = dangerous APIs + failure rules on
  comment/string-stripped code, plus structure (manifest, build.txt, namespaces = mod name, textures, ApiVersion,
  ctor, Dispose deregistering every hook, net9.0 target, write paths only under TShock.SavePath/Main.SavePath, no
  binaries/absolute paths, TShock/tModLoader never mixed, "Terraria" not in the mod name).
- **Real compile check (build host only):** `devhost run --lock -- bash scripts/cyrus/terraria-compile-check.sh`
  generates a 78-mod matrix (`scripts/cyrus/terraria-matrix.ts`: 26 prompts x 3 models) and compiles every one: TShock
  plugins with the .NET 9 SDK + the public TShock NuGet package, tModLoader mods with the .NET 8 SDK + the public
  tModLoader release, packaged into a real `.tmod` by tModLoader's own `-build`. Tools live in
  `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-terraria-tools` on node-2 (`--setup` reinstalls them). No game files are needed or used.
- **Tests:** `test/cyrus-game-terraria.test.ts` (pure).
- **Not done:** live load-test on a throwaway server, compile step inside the Cyrus build pipeline, a tModLoader
  server product. Checklist: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/game-terraria/READINESS.md`. The game stays "soon".
EOF

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
